$comment: Ratchet baseline for `npm run typecheck` (scripts/typecheck.mjs). Read that
script before editing this file: it is compared as an exact multiset of
(file, code, message), so it must be shrunk in the same commit that fixes an
entry, or `npm run typecheck` fails. Production src/ sources only - test
files and config files are never baselined.
`diagnostics` is generated from tsc 5.9.3's own output, never written by
hand; see 'Regenerating the baseline' in scripts/typecheck.mjs for the recipe
and for how to check a regeneration. tsconfig.json as committed by issue #39.
One entry, down from 16 - and the 15 that went were one missing line, not 15
small debts. src/services/types.ts imported five types from `@/lib/types`
and re-exported none of them, so the `export type { ... } from "@/lib/types"`
line that src/services/index.ts imports by name did not exist. Without it
those five types resolved to `any` inside `ClusterService` - hence the 5 x
TS2459 at the import site - and every service return type was `any`, which is
what produced the 10 x TS7006 implicit-any callback parameters in the route
components. Adding the one re-export removed all 15 at once and no route
component needed a change, so read this before 'fixing' a TS7006 in
src/routes/: the fix is one line in src/services/types.ts, not in the route.
The entry that remains is a real production bug rather than type debt.
src/services/index.ts wraps the synchronous `ClusterService.streamJobLogs`
in an `async` function, so the wrapper hands back `Promise<Unsubscribe>`.
src/routes/jobs.$jobId.tsx stores that in a `(() => void) | undefined` and
calls it from the effect cleanup, so leaving the page invokes a Promise and
leaks the log WebSocket. Fixing it deletes this entry and shrinks the file
to zero. It is deliberately NOT fixed by issue #39: it is a behaviour change
with its own review, not type debt, and #39 declined it on purpose.
It is tracked in issue #45.

diagnostics.message: Type 'Promise<Unsubscribe>' is not assignable to type '() => void'.
